def test(page):
    # Open Settings from the header gear icon
    page.click(1158, 40)
    # Go to the Accessibility category
    page.click(133, 325)

    # Precondition: settings chrome (title + category sidebar) is visible.
    page.expect_image(
        "acc-page-medium",
        region=[40, 95, 250, 650],
        threshold=0.1,
        max_diff_pixels=40,
        precondition=True,
    )

    # Open the Caption size picker and choose Large
    page.click(598, 439)
    page.click(640, 446)

    # Behavior: the built-in caption preview shows the Large reading size.
    page.expect_image(
        "caption-large-preview",
        region=[963, 155, 1222, 382],
        threshold=0.1,
        max_diff_pixels=60,
    )

I saved the test to `/workspace/output/test.py`. It hasn't been run: there was no way to execute it while writing it, so I don't know yet whether it passes on the correct app or catches a fault.

**What the test does:**
1. Clicks the gear icon to open Settings, then clicks **Accessibility**.
2. **Setup check:** compares the "Settings" title and the category list on the left against the screenshot `acc-page-medium`. This area doesn't change with caption size, so it only confirms the right screen was reached.
3. Opens **Caption size** and clicks **Large**.
4. **Main check:** compares the caption preview card on the right against the screenshot `caption-large-preview`. That card holds the "A world worth exploring." caption and its "Large captions" label. With Medium the caption fit on two short lines; after choosing Large it is clearly bigger. The pixel tolerance is small, so a preview that stays at Medium size won't match.

Two screenshots taken after choosing Large were identical, so the preview's star background doesn't appear to animate. All click positions come from my own screenshots.
